name: Anarcho-Naturism
summary: Anarcho-naturism (naturianism, libertarian naturism) fuses anarchism with a return to natural life. Its founders in 1890s Paris rejected every legally established power and politics, accepting only the laws of nature, and condemned industrial civilization, progress and machines as domineering, urging limited needs, self-sufficiency and nudism. It was a loose current that spread to Spain and Cuba, not a systematic programme.
scope: The French naturian current of Émile Gravelle, Henri Zisly and Henri Beylie (journals L'État Naturel, Le Naturien, La Vie Naturelle), with the Spanish and Cuban anarchist naturism it influenced. Excludes mainstream apolitical naturism and nudism as leisure, and later anarcho-primitivism. Most economic and social-policy questions are not addressed in the sources, so many answers are inferences from its anarchism and anti-industrialism.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage labour and legal regulation by a state are outside the naturian project of self-sufficient living; a wage floor is an inference from their rejection of legal power.

public-ownership.rationale: Naturians reject every legally established power, so state ownership of industry is excluded; they also oppose industrial infrastructure itself.

unions-good.rationale: Anarcho-naturists in Cuba and Spain moved among anarcho-syndicalist circles, but the naturians' own writings focus on a return to nature rather than industrial unions, so adherents are split or indifferent.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations are products of the industrial civilization they oppose, but regulation would be state action; adherents would want them gone rather than regulated.

cut-welfare.rationale: Naturians reject the state but nothing in the sources says they favour cutting welfare as a policy; the statement's dependency framing is foreign to them.

worker-ownership.rationale: Naturians placed themselves among moderate libertarians who set aside part of anarchist-communist doctrine; factory ownership matters little to a movement rejecting industry.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Opposition to all legally established power and politics makes state surveillance unacceptable.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Naturians included both temperate and abstinent members regarding alcohol and tobacco, so legal status of drugs is not a settled naturian position; anti-prohibition follows from anarchism but natural-health ideals pull the other way.

strong-leader.rationale: Zisly states naturians fight all legally established power; a leader bypassing gridlock is the opposite of their anarchism.

state-harmful.rationale: Zisly describes naturians as anarchists in politics, opposed to all legally established power and all politics, accepting only the laws of nature.

limit-guns.rationale: Anarchists oppose state monopoly of force but naturians say little about arms; some are revolutionaries and some not.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and military are instruments of the legal power naturians fight.

more-religion-public.rationale: Zisly says naturians are all materialists and rejects religious adherence; religion in public life is opposed, as is every established power.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: International bodies are legal powers above states; the naturian rejection of all legal power covers them.

nation-first.rationale: Anarchists reject the nation-state as an authority; naturians have no stated nationalism.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Zisly called progress and civilization absurd and saw machines as inherently domineering, and says victims of technology are victims of Progress.

revolution-justified.rationale: Zisly notes naturians included both revolutionaries and anti-revolutionaries, so support is not universal, but anarchist politics generally accepts revolution as justified.

experts-over-public.rationale: Naturians called themselves anti-scientific anarchists and reject authority, so rule by experts is rejected.

central-planning.rationale: Central planning is state power over industry; both the anarchism and the anti-industrialism of naturians reject it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protecting industry combines state action with the industrialism that Zisly opposed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of industry is rejected both as state power and as support for industrial civilization.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Anarchist communists in the movement wanted abolition, but Zisly described naturians as differing from anarchist communism on some points; not settled.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages are legal powers that naturians reject.

one-party-rule.rationale: Zisly states naturians oppose all legally established power and all politics, which excludes a ruling party.

democracy-best.rationale: Naturians oppose parliamentarism and all politics according to Zisly's account; they are not democrats in the representative sense.

direct-votes.rationale: Anarchists prefer voluntary consensus to voting under a state, but direct votes beat representation; split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Naturians accept no authority besides natural law and reject all established power.

political-violence-never.rationale: Naturians included revolutionaries and anti-revolutionaries, so views on violence were divided; absolute pacifism is not their stated line, though a pacifist current existed later.

war-builds-character.rationale: Naturism became associated with pacifism in Germany and anarchist naturists opposed war; the glorification of war conflicts with natural-life ideals.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Zisly accepts only the laws of nature, rejects religion, and rejects legal power.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Naturians are not market anarchists; they reject legal power in general, and no private-defence stance is documented.

military-superiority.rationale: Military power is a legal-authority structure opposed by naturians.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Zisly distanced naturians from the scientific claims of anarchist communism; not a stated naturian thesis.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political unions are legal powers that naturians oppose, and they denounce civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Naturian anarchism descended from individualist anarchism, but they stress harmony with nature, so adherents are split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Naturians reject externally imposed authority; duty-first communitarianism is not their ethic.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Naturians hold that the laws of nature are the only valid ones and that people should adapt themselves to nature rather than fight it, which points to valuing nature itself.

limit-population.rationale: Neo-Malthusian circles overlapped with anarchism, but population limits by the state would conflict with naturians' rejection of legal power.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Zisly opposed industrialization and machines and condemned progress and civilization as ignoble; Gravelle's naturianism set a free natural state against industrial civilization.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Zisly saw machines as inherently domineering and rejected progress, so speeding up technological change is the reverse of his aims.

human-enhancement.rationale: They call for adapting to nature, but they also stand for bodily freedom; enhancement through technology runs against their anti-technological outlook.

restore-past-order.rationale: Naturians looked back to a natural prehistoric state, not to a lost social order; the statement's traditional-order sense does not fit.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Naturians treat the laws of nature as a doctrine; pragmatism is not their outlook.

direct-action.rationale: They reject parliamentarism and all politics; Zisly says naturians fight established power and combine practical lifestyle action with propaganda.

means-match-ends.rationale: Zisly promoted limited needs and practical self-sufficient living as the way to a natural life, aligning means with the intended society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Zisly advocated a return to natural life with limited needs and self-sufficiency; naturian currents were nomadic and sedentary, and some saw prehistory as abundant, but not every adherent urged full foraging.

collective-farming.rationale: Both nomadic and sedentary naturians existed and self-sufficiency could be individual or communal; split.

taxation-theft.rationale: Anarchists reject the state and thus its taxes, though naturians made no known fiscal argument.

harm-principle.rationale: Anarchists reject state restriction broadly; naturians appeal to natural law rather than a harm principle.

conscription.rationale: Conscription is state coercion that naturians, opposed to all legally established power, reject.

state-as-business.rationale: They reject government itself, not a business model for it.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Naturians are anarchists who rejected hierarchy; nothing in sources endorses racial genetic hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation of any kind through bodies is political authority they reject.

national-rebirth.rationale: A nationalist theme alien to naturians who reject states and politics.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by oaths of loyalty is a legal power they reject.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labour is coercion opposed by all anarchists, including naturians.

universal-morality.rationale: They appeal to natural laws as universal, though the statement concerns reason-found moral truths; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Naturians reject political authority to define a common good.

rule-by-example.rationale: Naturians reject rulers altogether, whatever their example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anarchists reject states, yet decentralist sympathies exist; split.

force-without-un.rationale: Use of state military force abroad is opposed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Zisly called naturians anti-scientific anarchists who follow the laws of nature; they also reject religion, so emotion and nature, not reason alone, guide them.

class-collaboration.rationale: Zisly kept naturians apart from anarchist-communist doctrine and wrote nothing on class partnership or conflict, so no side is documented.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalism of workers is inconsistent with their anti-state outlook.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury law is not mentioned by Zisly or Gravelle; a legal ban is state action, while hostility to commerce pulls the other way, so it nets to neutral.

state-class-instrument.rationale: As anarchists who see legal power as the enemy, they would hold that the state serves domination, though the sources do not phrase it in class terms.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Industrial extraction is part of the industrial civilization Zisly opposed.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in any naturian source; anarchist egalitarian outlook rejects it.

proportional-representation.rationale: They reject parliamentary politics altogether, so voting reforms are not their goal.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading a government form by a state is contrary to their rejection of states.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State eugenics is coercive legal power that anarchists reject.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Naturians reject the state, so legal accountability is not their method.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Any state, even minimal, is a legally established power they oppose.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist debate about revolution and borders that the naturian sources never enter.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No naturian source discusses settlement or colonial states; the question is left without a documented answer.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Legal uniformity is a state project; anarchists reject civil law as such.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Zisly rejects religious adherence and legal power; law restricting belief is a coercion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Vegetarians and omnivores were both naturians, so no ban would be stated; a legal ban is also state power.

consent-of-governed.rationale: They accept no political authority as legitimate; consent theory does not fit.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export orientation belongs to industrial commerce they oppose.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Naturians reject progress itself and favour adaptation to nature.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: They oppose legal power over politics, and also reject party politics generally.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Zisly saw machines and powers as domineering and rejected legal authority, matching a freedom-from-domination view though not named.

separated-powers.rationale: They reject every legally established power rather than dividing it.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Legal restriction of labour action is state power they oppose.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship bureaucracy is a state power they reject.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: They reject representation, so the pay level is moot.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding party discipline is an organisational authority they reject.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: They reject sovereignty at all levels.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Zisly rejects religious adherence; no stance on church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerics holding authority are opposed by materialist anarchist naturians.

recall-officials.rationale: They reject offices; recall is moot.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Zisly urged a return to natural life, limited needs and self-sufficiency and condemned civilization; the naturist movement was built on health through nature and open air.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National unification through states is not their aim.

death-penalty.rationale: State execution is a legal power they reject.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Naturians are materialists and reject religious authority.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are state law they reject.

religious-exemptions.rationale: They oppose religion and law alike; exemptions are a legal construct.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International sovereign debt is a state-finance question absent from naturian writings.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The naturian sources do not treat national independence movements at all.

constituent-assembly.rationale: They oppose parliamentary politics and constitutions.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: They reject heads of state altogether.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims by states are not theirs.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: They reject both state and church; making the church subject to the state is not their method.

flat-income-tax.rationale: They reject taxation as part of the state.

space-expansion.rationale: Space programmes epitomise the progress and industry Zisly rejected.

mixed-constitution.rationale: They reject constitutions and political rule.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A debate internal to state socialism that naturians, distinct from anarchist communism, never joined.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Rejects both religious adherence and legal power.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Political unions among peoples are state-building.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority institutions within states are a nationality-policy question absent from naturian writings.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They reject courts and majority rule alike.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Self-sufficiency is a naturian ideal at personal level; a state economic bloc would not be.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Naturians had revolutionary and non-revolutionary members, so views on armed groups vary.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Opposition to all established power and privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Zisly called civilization and progress ignoble, so ruling others to civilise them is rejected, besides being domination.

patriotic-education.rationale: State schooling in loyalty is legal power and nationalism they reject.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Admissions and hiring policy is not a subject of the naturian sources.

public-money-creation.rationale: A state institution; they offer no monetary scheme.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutions are legal power; they accept only natural laws.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Naturians fight parliamentarism per Zisly's account of their politics.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Vegetarians were among naturians, but Zisly called vegetarianism anti-scientific and others ate meat, so this is an inference from nature-centred ethics.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Naturians included both vegetarians and omnivores according to Zisly, so views on animal use were split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hierarchical duty of the privileged is opposed to anarchist egalitarianism.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: No naturian source offers a theory of how ruling classes keep consent; they simply reject all established power.

native-born-offices.rationale: They reject public offices and legal citizenship.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Self-sufficiency is a naturian ideal, though applied to individuals not countries.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: They reject political leadership of any group.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Opposed to fascism as authoritarian, but they reject constitutions.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wage labour framing; they promote self-sufficiency over waged labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Imposed duties conflict with anarchist anti-authoritarianism.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private financial products are outside their self-sufficient lifestyle, and state pensions are rejected too.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: They reject parliament and the state budget.

single-official-language.rationale: State imposition of language is a legal power.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Zisly promoted limited needs and self-sufficiency and condemned civilization; the movement stressed simple living.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: A state military act they reject.

residents-only-property.rationale: A legal restriction by state authorities.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state employment programme, and wage employment in industry.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources do not take up this international-relations thesis; naturians reject parliamentary democracy while opposing war, so it is neutral.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Zisly states naturians recognise only natural law and oppose all legally established power, so legal duty to obey is denied.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not found in any source; contrary to anarchist egalitarianism.

public-access-to-information.rationale: They reject the state, so legal rights are not their frame.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Both are legal powers; neither is accepted.

religious-nation.rationale: Zisly says all naturians are materialists who reject religion, so defining a nation by religion has no place in their outlook.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-authoritarian and not anti-communist in a Cold War sense; hostile to state communism but not seeking its defeat.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Zisly rejects progress and civilization in the industrial commercial form.

socialized-care.rationale: Public services are state action; they favour self-sufficient living.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Claims of states or peoples to land are not accepted by anarchists.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Zisly's account has naturians fighting all legally established power, which rules out civil punishment of religious speech or practice.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Theocratic revolution is contrary to materialist naturians.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not found in any source; contrary to anarchist egalitarianism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: They are materialists who reject religious adherence and legal power.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: They reject the state; the statement concerns state rules that they would not make.

social-market-economy.rationale: A state-regulated industrial economy that they reject.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Military power is part of legal authority they fight, and naturism was linked with pacifism in Germany.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: They reject states and blocs; neutrality is an inference.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary rule is a legal power they fight.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The IMF and international lending are modern state-finance matters absent from the naturian sources.

property-franchise.rationale: They oppose legal voting systems and class restrictions.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: They recognise only natural laws and reject legal power.

online-participation.rationale: Online politics is both politics and technology that naturians reject.

citizens-assembly.rationale: They reject political deliberative bodies as a form of politics.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Naturians reject religion rather than reforming it, but the statement is about religious adherents.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: They fight established power and oppose commercial civilization; wealth as power would be included.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: They are materialists but reject state power, so state promotion is excluded.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: They oppose all legally established power, which includes police and prisons.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The sources do not rank charity against state aid, though mutual aid might fit anarchism.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: They reject religion, so not their issue.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: They reject legal marriage authority altogether; the statement presumes marriage law.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Views on violence varied among naturians, who included revolutionaries and anti-revolutionaries.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Zisly says all naturians are materialists.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Zionist-style homeland debates are not touched by the naturian sources.

god-not-male.rationale: Zisly rejects religion as such, so intra-religious debate about divine language is not their concern.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ethnic economic control is contrary to anarchism.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative unification by states is not theirs.

independent-unions.rationale: If unions exist, anarchist circles want them independent of the state; naturians themselves said little.

family-wage.rationale: Wage-based industrial framing; not their ideal.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Naturians favoured natural living and were anti-scientific per Zisly, and approvals are regulatory power.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Technological research funded by government is contrary to their anti-technology and anti-state views.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Untraceable payment is a modern question; naturians reject state control but also modern technology, so no side follows.

person-over-state.rationale: Individualist anarchists reject treating persons as means for the community; the state is rejected entirely.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Zisly states naturians are all materialists.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering is an industrial technology opposed to natural living.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: They reject armies altogether so the statement's premise is not accepted.

language-defines-nation.rationale: National unification is not their aim.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiracy nationalism contrary to their outlook.

pollution-taxes.rationale: They oppose industrial pollution but also taxation by the state.

future-generations.rationale: Nature-centred critique of civilization supports preserving the Earth.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The naturian sources make no claims about distinct values of women.

arms-reduction.rationale: Opposes armed state power but wants abolition rather than reduction.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: They oppose legally established power and its monopolies.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: State welfare and taxation they reject.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Legal rules by the state they reject.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Naturians included both nomadic and sedentary, both communal and individual lifestyles, implying tolerance for varied arrangements.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Treating nature as a commodity contradicts their view that people should adapt to nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Materialists and anarchists reject the sacred nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loans are a modern state-credit issue the sources never touch.

public-service-media.rationale: State-funded media; they reject state institutions.

workers-own-party.rationale: They oppose all politics, including parties.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic classification question with no connection to naturian writings.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Chiefs in lawmaking are a legal power.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Zisly's stress on natural life concerns freedom too; anarchists reject coercion for environment.

voter-id.rationale: They reject elections and state identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: They reject religion and legal recognition.

women-suffrage.rationale: They reject voting politics, though they would not deny women participation.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Legal power at an international level.

national-church-status.rationale: They reject religion and state privilege.

simple-living.rationale: Zisly promoted limited needs and self-sufficiency as the heart of a return to natural life.

equal-conscription.rationale: Naturians rejected military power and the state, and Zisly's circle opposed militarism, so 'or neither' applies and men-only conscription is rejected.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Naturians condemned machines and industrial progress, so combining advanced technology with tradition would not satisfy them.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: They rejected every legally established power and accepted only the laws of nature, so human-made unjust law has no claim on conscience.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Zisly and the naturians condemned machines and industrial progress as domineering, so maximising automation is the opposite of their aim.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: They refused all legal power and politics, so a party-led state of any kind, with or without markets, is incompatible with their anarchism.

missingStatements.text: People should live as simply and self-sufficiently as possible, keeping their needs limited.
missingStatements.rationale: Zisly promoted limited needs and self-sufficiency as the heart of a return to natural life.

missingStatements.text: Nudity in appropriate public settings is healthy and should be legally allowed.
missingStatements.rationale: Zisly defended nudism and naturist anarchists treated it as emancipatory, as Koch used it against authority.
missingStatements.declined: Too narrow: a single naturist practice that few other ideologies take a position on.

missingStatements.text: Machines and large-scale technology are inherently domineering over people.
missingStatements.rationale: Zisly saw machines as fundamentally domineering and opposed industrialization.

notes: Strands differed on diet (vegetarian and omnivore), settlement (nomadic and sedentary) and revolution, per Zisly. Spanish and Cuban anarchist naturism and German left naturism (Koch) are related but not the same current.
